purpose: Align historical static and browser contracts with the canonical Surface Standard runtime, and escalate any falsified runtime assumption into the effective standard rather than masking it in evidence consumers.

saturationImpact.reason: Historical alignment exposed a stable post-decision runtime rerender that lost terminal vocabulary; the finding adds one lexical primitive, one contradiction primitive and ICTC-L15.

invariants.name: semantic-token-declaration
invariants.rule: Historical design-system assurance must validate the declared CSS custom-property syntax --ds-ease:, not the invalid literal --ds-ease;.

invariants.name: progressive-settings-sequencing
invariants.rule: The browser journey must fill organization fields while the organization disclosure is open, then open the provider disclosure and fill provider fields.

invariants.name: progressive-job-sequencing
invariants.rule: The browser journey must open the criteria and schedule job groups before interacting with controls moved into those groups.

invariants.name: canonical-terminal-vocabulary
invariants.rule: Historical browser assertions must consume the terminal labels Accetta nel catalogo, Accettata nel catalogo and Scarica evidenza.

invariants.name: no-runtime-bypass
invariants.rule: Alignment must not force hidden controls, disable single-open behavior, modify server authority, or reintroduce legacy labels in production code.

invariants.name: same-head-evidence
invariants.rule: Historical-contract assurance, Surface Standard assurance, server-backed browser and general CI must execute against the same PR head before the slice is considered mature.

invariants.name: stable-post-toggle-observation
invariants.rule: Single-open browser assertions must observe the stable state after details toggle reconciliation closes the previous sibling; tests use bounded condition waiting rather than instantaneous counts or arbitrary sleeps.

invariants.name: direct-rerender-terminal-reconciliation
invariants.rule: When a human source decision directly reconstructs the source dialog after refresh, the runtime must emit ictc:surface-changed after reconstruction so terminal lexical and visual layers reconcile the stable DOM.

observedFailures.observation: enterprise-2-design-system-check expected --ds-ease; while the runtime declares --ds-ease:cubic-bezier(...).
browser-product-check opened provider after organization and then attempted to fill organizationName after single-open behavior had hidden that section.
The revised journey asserted an instantaneous open-section count while details toggle reconciliation was still closing the previous sibling.

The canonical decision action completed, but renderSourceDialog rebuilt base Verificata/Stato umano copy after the refresh-time terminal pass; Accettata nel catalogo never appeared in the stable source body.

preventiveAlignments.reason: authorities and sourceHints are owned by closed criteria/schedule groups and must be opened before interaction.
source acceptance/status and evidence-download assertions consume canonical terminal vocabulary and therefore expose any runtime regression back to legacy copy.

acceptance: The semantic-token historical check passes without changing the design-system CSS token declaration.
The product browser journey completes settings configuration through the single-open progressive disclosure contract.
The product browser journey completes job configuration by explicitly opening each required disclosure owner.
Single-open assertions wait for the stable post-toggle state using Playwright condition assertions rather than arbitrary sleeps.
After a human source decision, the direct source-dialog rerender emits ictc:surface-changed and stable post-decision copy remains canonical.
Source decision and event evidence assertions use canonical terminal labels.
No API permission, capability or backend authority is weakened by this slice.
Surface Standard assurance, server-backed UI-standard browser, historical browser journeys, contract audit, runtime E2E and security are re-evaluated on the same final PR head.
claimBoundary: This model demonstrates historical-contract alignment and the runtime correction falsified by that alignment. It does not establish universal regression freedom, accessibility conformance, legal compliance, certification or production readiness.
